note: Every mock provider payload this repo can put on the wire carries at least one of
these tokens, in a field a person reads on screen or in the raw response body.
The point is that a fixture which escapes its test is recognisable as fake at a
glance, by a person or by a script, instead of looking like a booking someone can
make. See docs/ACCEPTANCE.md, 'Never ship a flight that does not exist'.
Consumers: tools/probe-results.mjs refuses to report an itinerary count when it
finds a token in the page or in a provider response, and tests/e2e/guard.spec.ts
fails the suite when a fixture file under tests/e2e/fixtures/ carries none.
flightNumbers is the whole pool a mock may draw from. ZZ is not an assigned IATA
airline designator and no airline numbers a flight 0000, so every one of these is
impossible rather than merely unused. Reusing one across specs is fine: they are
markers, not identities. Add more if you run out.
